meta.title: Pin supply-chain metadata and publish verifiable artifacts
meta.author: Codex manager

feature.problem_statement: Mutable workflow action refs, unpinned build/migration images, missing dependency automation and Go vulnerability coverage, and absent SBOM/provenance publication reduce confidence that released artifacts correspond to reviewed source.
goals: Pin every external/internal action and governed production image to reviewed immutable identifiers.
Add reviewable dependency update configuration and a reproducible Go vulnerability gate.
Generate SBOM/provenance metadata tied to exact release digests and document verification.
Make platform-dependent signature/referrer prerequisites explicit rather than claiming unverified deployment enforcement.
non_goals: Inventing private action SHAs, image digests, signing keys, or registry capabilities.
Adding standalone binary release artifacts that the repository does not currently publish.
Changing Argo admission policy or Nexus configuration without platform-owner evidence.
scope_in: CI/release action refs, Dockerfile and chart migration image references.
Supply-chain checker/tests, Dependabot configuration, and pinned govulncheck invocation.
Release SBOM/provenance/signing wiring only where verified platform prerequisites exist, plus safe documentation and explicit fail-closed prerequisites.
scope_out: Deployment admission enforcement without platform approval

requirements.statement: All GitHub Action references in CI and release workflows, including private Codicarium actions, must use reviewed full commit SHAs with a human-readable release comment.
requirements.rationale: Mutable tags allow trusted build behavior to change without a repository diff.

requirements.statement: Production Dockerfile bases and governed chart/CI migration images must use verified immutable multi-architecture digest references; a supply-chain checker must reject mutable or empty governed references.
requirements.rationale: Build and migration inputs must resolve to reviewed content across supported architectures.

requirements.statement: Repository configuration must provide reviewable automated updates for GitHub Actions, Go modules, npm, and Docker inputs, and CI must run a reproducibly pinned Go vulnerability check alongside existing tests/vet/audit.
requirements.rationale: Pinned inputs need a safe update path and language-appropriate vulnerability coverage.

requirements.statement: Release metadata must include an SBOM for published image/chart contents and provenance tied to GITHUB_SHA and immutable artifact digests, or fail closed with an explicit documented platform prerequisite when the target registry cannot store/verify attestations.
requirements.rationale: Consumers need verifiable component and source-to-artifact evidence rather than an undocumented promise.

requirements.statement: Deployment documentation must describe digest, SBOM, provenance, and signature verification and identify Nexus referrer, signer identity, and Argo/admission prerequisites as external gates when not verified.
requirements.rationale: Repository changes cannot substitute for platform trust configuration.

acceptance_criteria.scenario: Given CI and release workflow YAML, when the supply-chain checker runs, then every action uses a reviewed full SHA and retains a release comment.
Given Dockerfile, chart, and governed CI image references, when checker/tests run, then mutable tags or empty digests fail and verified multi-architecture digests pass.
Given a clean checkout, when CI runs, then Dependabot configuration is discoverable and the pinned govulncheck command executes reproducibly.

Given a release digest, when release metadata is generated, then SBOM/provenance is tied to that digest and source SHA; unsupported registry/signing prerequisites fail closed with an actionable reason.
Given deployment documentation, when an operator verifies an artifact, then the exact digest/SBOM/provenance/signature procedure and external platform prerequisites are clear.

test_plan.approach: Parse workflow refs and governed image references; reject tags, missing SHAs, empty digests, malformed/mismatched architectures.
Validate Dependabot ecosystems and run pinned govulncheck fixture/command without @latest or mutable installer.
Exercise SBOM/provenance generation with synthetic immutable digest and verify subject SHA/digest; use a negative unsupported-referrer fixture.
Run docs/workflow parsing, actionlint, full CI, and diff/credential scans; inspect verification runbook for external gates.

review_checks: Every action SHA verified against upstream tag commit
Docs distinguish repository and platform responsibilities

perspectives.summary: Split repository-verifiable pinning/scanning from Nexus signing and Argo enforcement prerequisites; avoid unverifiable claims.
Require exact action commits, multi-architecture image digests, fail-closed reference checks, and no mutable vulnerability installer.
Demand negative fixtures, release-subject digest linkage, full CI, and independent platform capability evidence.

council.consensus_summary: Implement the repository-side supply-chain controls now, and leave signed attestation/deployment enforcement explicitly gated on verified Nexus and identity capabilities.
open_questions: Does Nexus support OCI referrers for image/chart SBOMs and signatures?
Which signer identity/OIDC or KMS path is approved for release?
Can private Codicarium action SHAs be kept stable through the update process?
